headline: No bail for alleged Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of Australia’s ‘febrile’ political environment

members.title: No bail for alleged Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of Australia’s ‘febrile’ political environment
members.lead: AFP commissioner says MPs are generally concerned about growing volume of abuse and intimidation Follow our live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The head of the Australian federal police has condemned a “febrile” political environment that has seen one person charged every week over the alleged threatening of MPs, as Victoria announces new steps to protect politicians. But the AFP and Victoria police insist they had no intelligence to suggest 43-year-old Brendan Nugent would go on to allegedly drive a Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP Helen Haines in a targeted attack. members.title: AFP warns Australia of ‘tsunami of youth crime’ and radicalisation accelerated by AI
members.lead: Children as young as 12 among dozens subject to federal police operations since 2020, parliamentary inquiry hears Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast Australia is facing a “tsunami” of youth crime as artificial intelligence accelerates the pace and scale of radicalisation, a parliamentary inquiry has heard. The Australian federal police acting deputy commissioner Sandra Booth told the hearing on Wednesday that, while radicalisation had traditionally taken years or months, that process could now happen within days. members.title: Helen Haines has lost both legs after alleged attack but ‘her heart and mind are in good shape’, husband says
members.lead: Haines is in stable condition. Surgeons tried to save her right leg but both have now been amputated due to injuries Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast The independent MP Helen Haines has lost both legs but remains in a stable condition, two days after an alleged targeted attack near her electorate office in north-east Victoria. Haines, the federal MP for Indi, had been in a critical but stable condition after she was struck by a car in Wangaratta on Monday afternoon. Surgeons were trying to save her right leg on Tuesday, but both legs had to be amputated due to the seriousness of her injuries. Continue reading...
